citation: Qian, C., Cong, X., Yang, C., Chen, W., Su, Y., Xu, J., ... & Yang, D. (2023). ChatDev: Communicative agents for software development. arXiv:2307.07924.
notes: Large effect with GPT-3.5-era models. MAS quality 0.395 vs SAS 0.142. Diminishes with stronger models.

citation: Chen, Y., Li, J., & Zhang, W. (2025). Single-agent or multi-agent systems? Why not both? arXiv:2505.18286.
design: Within-subjects crossed (same tasks, MAS vs SAS)
notes: MAS advantage shrinks from 10% to 3% with Gemini-2.0-Flash. Conservative estimate for modern models.

citation: Schultz, A., Bergmann, L., & Kupper, C. (2026). Personality, role, and expressive style in large language models: An interactionist analysis. arXiv:2605.28037.
design: Within-subjects factorial (6 personality x 3 role x 3 style)
outcome: Personality x Role interaction (median across Big Five traits)
notes: Median omega-squared = 0.025 across traits. Range: 0.000 (Extraversion) to 0.200 (Conscientiousness). Converted f = sqrt(w2/(1-w2)).

citation: Yao, Y., Zhang, Y., & Chen, X. (2026). LLM-augmented digital twin for policy evaluation in short-video platforms. arXiv:2603.11333.
design: 2x2 factorial (template vs LLM persona x template vs LLM caption)
outcome: Session watch time (persona main effect ~16% change)
notes: Persona main effect; interaction with caption was near-zero.
